M. Forster’s “The Machine Stops” (1909) foretold how our problematic relationship with technology would develop.** **In January 1908, a year before the story was published, Forster wrote in his diary that rather than freeing us, science was enslaving us, especially new ‘machines’. He was, at the very least, a technosceptic, if not a full-on technophobe.** **In the future, Mankind dwells underground where they rely on *the Machine* for all their needs. Everyone owns a book, known as ‘the Book’, which is not the Bible (a bible in fact, yes) but rather a sort of instruction manual telling people about the Machine.** **The narrator tells us that the ‘clumsy business of public gatherings had been long since abandoned’. People stay in their own rooms, under the ground, and interact via technology – living a virtual rather than face-to-face existence in both their education and socialising.** **People ‘isolate themselves’ when they go to sleep, unplugging themselves from this technological world of telecommunication.** **They are allowed up to the surface, but only under supervised and permitted conditions.** **The inhabitants do not merely *use* the Machine. They inhabit a world whose entire structure is provided by it: communication, education, entertainment, information, social relations and material survival. Direct contact with other people becomes unnecessary; direct experience of the physical world becomes almost strange.** **"The Book” becomes authoritative; questioning the system becomes socially unacceptable; people begin venerating the Machine.** **The Machine does not need to become conscious or deliberately enslave humanity.** **The Machine, which everyone is now wholly dependent on slows down and grinds to a halt.** **Then the whole communication system shuts down.** **The story sees humanity helplessly come to an end as the machine they became over reliant on...** **Collapses.** **Lets think about the Human beings...** **The machines are making.** \-\-\-\-\- **As always, you can perfectly participate in the debate without knowing the story, but if you want here a some links...** [E.M. title: #16 Lisbon GenAI Meetup | Lisbon GenAI x AI.PT x AI Lisbon @Riskified Lisbon
description: ## **The Lisbon GenAI Community is back for Meetup #16** This time, we’re joining forces with **AI.PT and AI Lisbon** for an evening focused on what happens when AI agents move beyond demos and start interacting with real-world systems. From turning the **browser itself into an API** to rethinking **how AI agents should be operated, controlled and designed around humans**, two speakers will share very different perspectives on what it takes to make agents useful in production. **🗓️ October 20th\, 2026 \| 18:30 \| Riskified Lisbon** A big thank you to **Riskified** for hosting us, and to **AI.PT, AI Lisbon and synvert xgeeks** for helping bring the community together. *** ### 📅 Agenda **18:30 — Check-in, Drinks & Networking** **19:00 — Opening & Community Intro** Lisbon GenAI Community · AI.PT · AI Lisbon · Riskified ### **19:15 — 🎤 Talk 1: The Browser is the API** **Robert Berglund — Senior Software Engineer @ Riskified** *Abstract:* Every new payment gateway used to mean the same thing for us: learn its API, map its payloads, handle its web-hooks, test it, and maintain it forever. Some gateways don't even offer an API, so for those the answer was a manual process. What if we could integrate with every gateway through one universal API instead? In this talk, we'll cover how we built an AI agent that uses the portal like a human does, and how onboarding a gateway went from a development project to a config entry. By the end of the talk, you'll learn how it works, what it took to run it unattended in production, how you can do it yourself, and where the line sits between what you let a model do and what stays plain code. ### **19:50 — 🎤 Talk 2: Please do not touch — Running AI agents like a museum runs a collection** **André Gonçalves — Head of Innovation & Growth @ synvert xgeeks** *Abtract:* A museum is an operating system for the moments that matter. AI agents will soon be as common as artworks, and just as dependent on what surrounds them. Museums quietly solved that before anyone said “agent”, so this talk is a guided tour: **six rooms, a few incidents, and an exit through the gift shop.** It borrows their answers with slightly more confidence than the comparison deserves, and ends with the question every leader now faces: **Are you optimising for fewer humans, or for better human moments?** ### **20:25 — 🍕 Pizza, Drinks & Networking** Stay around after the talks for pizza, drinks and conversations with the Lisbon AI community. *** **Entrance is free, but spots are limited — grab your ticket and join us.** See you at **Riskified Lisbon** 👋 **Communities & Partners:** Lisbon GenAI Community · AI.PT · AI Lisbon · synvert xgeeks · Riskified

description: Before Monsanto became the lush green lung of Lisbon, it was a desolate, windswept hill. Today, those saplings have grown into a majestic, thriving ecosystem—a living testimony to the land’s power to heal and regenerate. Join us on **Saturday, October 24,** for our **final walk of the season before our winter break** in Italy. Together, we will walk gentle forest paths, pause under the autumn canopy to attune to the shifting energy of the woods, and reflect on what it means to rebuild, restore, and bloom after times of exhaustion. This walk is not about logging miles, building speed, or pushing fitness.
